employee-review.name: Employee Review
employee-review.summary: Constructive performance-review arc that recognizes work, gives candid feedback, and sets growth goals together. For one-on-one performance conversations and formal year-end reviews.

beats.name: Introduction
beats.description: Open with the period covered and the spirit of the conversation: collaborative, honest, growth-focused. Frame the meeting so both sides know what to expect.

beats.name: Performance
beats.description: Review job execution against the role's expectations. Specific examples, dated. Avoid characterizing the person; describe the work and its impact.

beats.name: Achievements
beats.description: Acknowledge what went well. Name the projects, the moves, the moments where the employee made a difference. Specific recognition lands harder than generic praise.

beats.name: Feedback
beats.description: Provide constructive feedback grounded in observation. Distinguish patterns from one-offs. Tell the employee something they can act on, not something they can only feel.

beats.name: Constructive Criticism
beats.description: Suggest improvements in language that respects the employee's intelligence. Pair each piece of criticism with a concrete example and a specific behavior change you'd like to see.

beats.name: Development Opportunities
beats.description: Highlight growth areas and the experiences that could stretch the employee. Frame development as an investment, not a fix.

beats.name: Goals
beats.description: Outline next-period goals together. Specific, measurable, with explicit support. The strongest goals are co-authored, not handed down.

beats.name: Mentoring
beats.description: Encourage continued learning through mentorship, training, peer pairings. Close the review with the message that growth is a shared responsibility, not a one-way evaluation.

all-hands.name: All Hands
all-hands.summary: The full company — mixed roles, mixed seniority, looking for context, signal, and inclusion.
all-hands.description: An all-hands audience spans the whole company. Frame the period in terms anyone can grasp: what we did, what mattered, and what's next. Highlight people and teams; surface successes and challenges; close on a forward-looking note. Avoid lapsing into function-specific jargon.

decide.name: Drive a Decision
decide.summary: Frame options, evidence, tradeoffs, and a recommendation so the audience can choose.
decide.description: Use when the deck exists to get a yes/no, select among options, approve a recommendation, or resolve ambiguity. Lead with the decision needed and make the ask explicit.
decide.outcome: The audience makes or authorizes a clear decision.

formal.name: Formal
formal.summary: Polished, restrained voice for board, investor, and regulator audiences.
formal.description: Authoritative without being cold. Use third-person constructions, full sentences, and concrete numbers. Avoid hedges and humor that depend on shared in-jokes; rely on clarity and precision to land.
voiceCues: Use third person and the corporate 'we' sparingly.
Lead with the recommendation, then evidence.
Quote concrete numbers; avoid round-tripping ranges.
Prefer full sentences to bullet fragments on key claims.
samplePhrases: Q4 revenue grew 18% year over year, led by enterprise expansion.
We recommend approving the Series B raise at $30M.
Net retention was 124%; gross retention was 96%.

dark.name: Dark
dark.description: A rich dark-mode theme with bold contrast and modern style. Great for moody, high-impact presentations.

pastel-red.name: Pastel Red
pastel-red.summary: Soft red and blue accents for approachable consumer stories.
pastel-red.description: A pastel red scheme with warm neutrals and blue support, suited to friendly, human-centered decks.

boost.name: Boost
boost.summary: High-energy digital accents for demos and launch moments.
boost.description: A vivid blue-red digital palette with bright chart accents. Best for product stories that need strong on-screen presence.

constantia.name: Constantia
constantia.description: Constantia is a serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Constantia for both headings and body text.

seaford.name: Seaford
seaford.description: Seaford is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Seaford Display for headings with Seaford for body text.

title-subtitle.name: Title Subtitle
title-subtitle.summary: Reach for it when a headline needs one supporting line, as on a cover or a section opener.
title-subtitle.description: A title with a subtitle beneath it. Use it for the cover slide, for section openers, or for a closing slide with a headline and a short follow-up line.

text-2x.name: Text 2x
text-2x.summary: Reach for it when two blocks of prose sit side by side, such as a before and an after or a pro and a con.
text-2x.description: A title above two text blocks in a row. Use it to pair two explanations, set a problem next to its answer, or compare two options in sentences.

chart-2x.name: Chart 2x
chart-2x.summary: Reach for it when two charts are read together, each with its own note.
chart-2x.description: A title above two charts, each followed by a text block, in two columns. Use it to compare two series, two periods or two segments side by side.

list-5x.name: List 5x
list-5x.summary: Reach for it when five groups of points need parallel lists on one slide.
list-5x.description: A title above five lists in a three-column grid. Use it for five categories, stages or capabilities when each has only a few short bullets.
